spots.name: Snowshoe Peak
spots.tip: A notable summit. Check the road and trail first; first and last light on high ground is the reason to go, and it's often the subject from below. Summit 2,663 m (8,738 ft).

spots.name: Kootenai National Forest
spots.tip: Wildlife is most active in the first two hours after sunrise. Stay on trails, use your car as a blind on auto routes and give animals space.

spots.name: Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Bridge
spots.tip: A landmark bridge: try blue hour when the lights come on, or low side light that shows the structure.

spots.name: Alvord Lake
spots.tip: A lake: calm air at dawn gives mirror reflections, and mist often sits on the water on cold mornings. The pin marks the middle of the lake: pick a shore spot facing the light.

spots.name: Swinging Bridge
spots.tip: A landmark with history. Low light brings out texture; check opening hours if it's fenced.

spots.name: Bull River wetland
spots.tip: eBird birding hotspot with 125 species recorded. Birds are most active in the first two hours after sunrise; recent sightings at ebird.org/hotspot/L1486456.

spots.name: Garver Mountain Lookout Tower
spots.tip: A lookout tower or fire lookout: a full-circle view, so it works at sunrise and sunset. Many are staffed in summer and some can be rented.

spots.name: Leigh Creek Falls
spots.tip: Best under soft overcast or in shade so the highlights don't blow out. A slow shutter (1/4–1 s on a tripod) smooths the water; flow peaks after rain and snowmelt.

spots.name: Libby Dam
spots.tip: A mapped viewpoint. Check which way it faces: east for sunrise, west for sunset. Arrive 30 minutes early to scout foreground.

spots.name: Dodge Summit
spots.tip: A mountain pass: easy high ground by car. Fog often fills the valleys on either side at sunrise; check winter road conditions.
